title: DRAM price per GB, 1990-2024, with AI Impacts fitted decline rates
conventions: McCallum table lists $/Mbyte at irregular (monthly-ish) dates. Annual value = geometric mean of that calendar year's entries, x1000 to $/GB. Nominal dollars (McCallum's table); AI Impacts fitted CPI-adjusted 2020 dollars, so fitted rates are not recomputed from this series. Table values are printed, so no chart read.

aiimpacts.cite: A. Bergal, AI Impacts 2020, 'Trends in DRAM price per gigabyte'

fits.note: 10x every 5.8 yr; data digitised by AI Impacts from a Jim Handy graph (WebPlotDigitizer)

break_note: AI Impacts splits at 2010; Handy (Memory Guy, 2019-11-20) says 'about 2011 or so' (via notes/q3, not re-read).

extraction.agent_b: extractor B, blind; parsed McCallum table from Wayback HTML

caveats: Live jcmit.net returned an unrelated (casino spam) page to curl on 2026-10-03; series taken from a Wayback capture of the genuine page, which ends mid-2024. No 2025-2026 points, so the 2026 price spike is not shown.

Series is nominal USD; AI Impacts fits are on CPI-adjusted 2020 USD. Our own OLS on the individual dated entries (nominal, log-linear): {"1991-2009": -38.4, "2010-2024.5": -12.3, "1991-2024.5": -28.6} %/yr, shown only as a sanity check, not for the slide; they differ from the published fits (different fit window/deflator).
The 2010+ series is non-monotonic (rise 2012-2014, 2016-2018, 2021) and the post-2010 fits are averages.
Objective Analysis data are not independently available; AI Impacts notes they may share sources with McCallum.
$/GB uses 1000 MB/GB; 1024 would raise every value 2.4%.
